entry.title: Furigana over the words a word list could not decide
entry.content:
Furigana over the words a word list could not decide

The button was drawing nothing over 人, 中, 日, 上 and the rest of the
words that are read two ways - which on an N5 paper is most of the kanji
on the page, so it read as a button that does not work. It was working:
the table is keyed by surface and can hold one reading per word, and for
those words it deliberately holds none.

A longer key can hold what a shorter one cannot. The table now also
carries a word with its kana neighbours - 人が ひとが, 中で なかで, 時まで
じまで, and the inflections that decide 来ます from 来なく - taken from the
tokenizer's own reading of that word in that sentence. 17,632 of them,
and the player already matched longest-first, so context wins wherever it
is listed.

Only kana neighbours, and only particles, auxiliaries, or a suffix the
tokenizer has already analysed as part of the word. Joining two kanji
words and concatenating their readings gets 二人 wrong (ににん, where the
word is ふたり), 三百 wrong (さんひゃく for さんびゃく) and 水よう日 wrong
(the tokenizer reads that 水 as みず): rendaku and 熟字訓 live at that
seam. And a key carrying kana matches only where its kanji edge stands
alone, or 人が would read 三人が and 4人が as ひと.

Measured per kanji against the tokenizer over 77,000 annotations on
twenty papers: 406 more correct readings, 9 more wrong ones, 415 fewer
words left bare. The share of shown readings that are the tokenizer's is
unchanged at 99.7%. Ruby on a rendered paper: N5 170 -> 193, N4 614 ->
659, N1 670 -> 681.

entry.title: The site is allowed to frame its own pages again
entry.content:
The site is allowed to frame its own pages again

"This content is blocked" in a phone preview was the site's own policy
refusing the site's own page. Chrome names the directive:

  Framing 'https://nihongomock.com/exam.html?id=n2-2010-07' violates the
  following Content Security Policy directive: "frame-src
  https://drive.google.com https://*.google.com ..."

frame-src was added for the Drive and YouTube players. Naming a directive
replaces what default-src was providing for it, so listing those hosts
silently dropped the 'self' that default-src 'self' had been giving - and
any iframe pointing at one of the site's own pages was refused. Anything
that embeds the site in a frame of its own hits it: a mobile preview
extension, which is where this turned up, and the first load surviving
while every navigation after it failed.

frame-src now lists 'self' first. Nothing else about the policy changes;
frame-ancestors still refuses everyone but the site itself.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: The box you press is the box the player arrives in
entry.content:
The box you press is the box the player arrives in

It was a white panel with a small button in it, which read as an empty
gap in the bar and then swapped itself for a black player. Now the idle
control is that player's box: 68px, #1e1e1e, a white arrow and "Play the
recording". Nothing changes size or colour when the recording loads.

And the wait before it plays is shorter by the handshake. Most of that
wait is Google's page and is not ours to shorten, but a cold press was
also paying for a DNS lookup, a TCP connection and a TLS negotiation with
a host the browser had never spoken to. warmDrive() opens those with
rel="preconnect" as the listening section is drawn, so they are paid
while the reader is still on the instructions.

Measured on a desktop connection, click to the frame's load event: 1359ms
cold, 1235ms warm, medians of four. On a phone the saving is larger - a
handshake there is round trips, not milliseconds.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: On a phone the player docks under the command bar, as it should
entry.content:
On a phone the player docks under the command bar, as it should

It was floating in the middle of the questions there. The stylesheet
placed it at --header-h + --bar-h, which is where the command bar ends
only while the site header is sticky. On a phone the header is not: it
scrolls away and the command bar sticks to the top of the window on its
own, so the sum put the player 109px below where it docks.

floatSync() already measures that edge to decide which bar to float, so
it now publishes it as --dock-h and the stylesheet uses that. Measured
rather than added up, and there is no arrangement of the chrome it can be
wrong about: 90px on a phone, 144 on a desktop, both exactly the command
bar's own bottom.

The idle player also stopped reserving the height of a player it has not
loaded. An empty 68px white box with a Play button adrift in it was a
third of the bar on a phone; the bar is 79px now, from 112, and 50 on a
desktop, from 83. The live frame keeps its 68.

entry.title: The controls sit in the middle, the bar is pinned from the start
entry.content:
The controls sit in the middle, the bar is pinned from the start

Three things, all on the listening paper.

The player's controls were sitting high in their box with a gap under
them. That is Drive's doing: it keeps about 17px of empty page below the
controls, so they land 8px above the middle of whatever box it is given -
measured at 68, 76 and 140px, a fixed strip rather than a proportion. The
frame is pushed down 8px to put them back in the middle, and the strip
that uncovers at the top is painted #1e1e1e, sampled from Drive's own
page, so the join cannot be seen.

The bar now follows you down the paper from the start, with nothing
pressed. It used to wait until it was playing, on the grounds that a Play
button trailing you down the page is clutter - but on a listening paper
the Play button is the thing you are reaching for, and scrolling back to
the head of the 問題 to find it is the greater clutter. Same for the
YouTube stand-in on the papers where it is the only audio there is.

And the word meanings now cover a listening question completely: the
options recovered from the transcript, which had never been read at all,
and the transcript itself with every filter off. A reading passage keeps
the level filter - it runs to hundreds of words and is on the page to be
read again - but a transcript is the only place the spoken words can be
seen, and the words worth naming there are the ordinary ones that went
past too fast. A noun and its suffix are also joined now when the pair is
a headword: 消費者 was being explained as 消費, 必要性 as 必要.

Per listening question on n2-2014-07: 28 words, now 38. Kanji of the
recovered options that fall inside a glossed word: 92.9%, from 91.2%.

entry.title: One player height, and a smaller one, with nothing cropped
entry.content:
One player height, and a smaller one, with nothing cropped

The size button is gone. It was there because the two players Drive can
draw want different room and a cross-origin frame will not say which one
arrived - but a reader should not have to fix the page's layout, and the
answer was in the wrong direction anyway: both players fit in 76px, which
is simply more than a strip of chrome should take from a bar that docks
at the top of the screen.

So the frame is still laid out at the 76px a whole player needs, and the
whole frame is then scaled to 68. Shorter without cutting anything off,
which a shorter frame would have done - 76px of player through a 68px
window is 8px of missing controls, the bug this bar started with. On a
phone the bar is 113px now, from 148.

entry.title: The player box is smaller, and its height is the reader's to set
entry.content:
The player box is smaller, and its height is the reader's to set

I had been sizing the box to the player my own browser gets. Signed out of
Google, Drive draws a compact control strip and 76px is exactly right for it.
Signed in - which is most people in Chrome, and is what your screenshots show -
it draws a waveform display instead, which wants more room and is squeezed into
76. The frame is cross-origin. Nothing on this side can ask which one arrived,
so no single number is right for everyone, and every number I picked was right
for one of us and wrong for the other.

So the height is a control now, next to the player: Smaller takes the box from
96px to 76, Bigger puts it back, the choice is remembered, and it moves every
recording on the paper at once - they come from one account, so they are the
same player. It appears only once something is playing; there is nothing to
resize before that.

And both containers are tighter than they were. The blue bar around the player
was 10px of padding and a 14px gap; it is 7 and 10. The box inside it was 112px;
it is 96. On a phone the player, its label and the size button were three
stacked rows, which is a third of the screen for a strip of chrome - the label
keeps its line and takes the button with it now, and the whole bar is 148px
instead of 180.

Checked at 1280 and 390 on n2-2010-07: 96px by default, 76 after one press,
both remembered and applied to all five recordings, and the button hidden until
a recording is running. Nothing else moved - zero frames until a play button is
pressed, two distinct labels where a paper has both recordings, 問題1 to 問題2
to 問題4 handing over as you scroll, no horizontal overflow, five site pages and
four papers N1-N5 with no console errors, furigana and scripts unchanged.

entry.title: One number for the player box, and it is the compact one
entry.content:
One number for the player box, and it is the compact one

96px was the wrong way to stop the cropping. It stops it, but Drive reads the
extra room as an invitation and draws its waveform display instead of its
control strip - bigger, slower to read, and no better for finding your place
in a listening test. You are right that it came out worse.

The strip is the player worth having: a round play button, a scrubber, the
time, a volume control, on black. Drive lays that out for 76px, so 76px is the
number - and it is one number, used for both the iframe and the window it is
seen through. That is what was actually broken. The frame was 76 and the
window 60, and a player drawn to fit 76 does not survive being shown through
60 of them: the top of the play button was simply outside the box. Neither
number meant anything on its own; only the gap between them did.

So there is no crop, and nothing to keep in step: --drive-h in exam.css is
read by the stylesheet and handed to the iframe when it is created.

Checked at 1280 and 390 on n2-2010-07: the strip draws in full, black, play
button whole, 117px for the whole bar on a phone rather than 137. Nothing else
moved - zero frames until a play button is pressed, two distinct labels where
a paper carries both recordings, the handover from 問題1 to 問題2 to 問題4 as
you scroll, no horizontal overflow, five site pages and four papers N1-N5 with
no console errors.

entry.title: The player is not cropped any more
entry.content:
The player is not cropped any more

The cut-off play button is a window we were holding too small, and it has been
wrong for longer than the recent changes - it is not new, it is just newly
visible now that the players are pressed rather than sitting there loading.

The frame was 60px onto a 76px iframe. The 16px difference was measured, on
three recordings, as empty field below Drive's controls, so cropping it took
the black box down to the part that had a player in it. That measurement holds
for one of Drive's two players. Signed in to a Google account, the preview
draws a taller layout instead - a waveform with a large round play button - and
60px cuts the top off that button. It does not read as a cropped player. It
reads as a broken one.

Which of the two a reader gets is decided inside a frame we cannot see into,
on Google's side, from their account and their experiments. So the window has
to fit the larger of them: the frame is 96px now, the iframe is told the same
height rather than carrying a number of its own, and whatever Drive draws is
shown whole. Both players lay out inside it - the compact strip centres, the
waveform one fits - and the two numbers can no longer drift apart, because
there is one of them.

Checked at 1280 and 390 on n2-2010-07, which has a recording in every 問題: the
round play button is whole, the 問題5 recording now takes its turn floating
where the shorter bar used to fall out of range, and there is no horizontal
overflow on a phone. Press-to-load, the labels, the scripts, the furigana and
the recovered options are all unchanged: zero frames until a play button is
pressed, two distinct labels where a paper has both recordings, 問題1 to 問題2
to 問題4 to 問題5 handing over as you scroll, five site pages and four papers
N1-N5 with no console errors.

entry.title: No black boxes: the recording is fetched when it is asked for
entry.content:
No black boxes: the recording is fetched when it is asked for

The black rectangle is Drive's own player. The frame is cross-origin, so what
is inside it - its colours, its controls, its playback speed - is Google's
page, and we are looking at it through a window. It cannot be restyled, and
the only way round it would be to play the file ourselves, which Drive refuses:
cross-origin-resource-policy: same-site on every byte.

What was ours to fix is that the window was being opened whether or not anybody
wanted it. A frame per 問題, drawn at render time, is five Google pages loading
at once on a paper with a recording each - so a listening paper opened as a row
of black rectangles, loading, for recordings nobody had asked to hear. That is
also the answer to why it sits there at first: five of them are queueing.

Now the player is a button in the paper's own colours, and the frame is created
by the click that asks for it - the same way the YouTube bar has always worked.
The click is a user gesture, which is what lets autoplay through, so pressing it
plays rather than loading a second play button to press. While the frame is
arriving the box says "Starting the player..." instead of sitting there black;
a cross-origin frame tells us nothing about its contents but it does say when it
has loaded, which is all that notice needs.

And a player only follows the reader down the page once it is playing something.
Before that it is a Play button, and a Play button that follows you around is
clutter - the rule the YouTube bar already followed.

**Both rows said the same thing.** On the 33 papers that carry a full upload as
well as their own recording, the whole-test bar and the YouTube bar both read
"Full recording - whole listening test", because I had given the paper's own
file the YouTube bar's label. The paper's own one now says "Audio for the whole
test", and drops the tag that was repeating it.

n2-2010-07 in the second screenshot was right, incidentally: five recordings,
one per 問題, 7:02 for 問題1 - so "Audio for this section - 問題1" is what it is.
Only papers with a single file get the whole-test treatment, and there the file
is the 41-minute one.

Checked in Chrome. n2-2010-07: five play buttons, zero frames until one is
pressed, then one frame and the notice. n2-2014-07: two rows, two different
labels, no frame until asked. Floating unchanged once started - the whole-test
recording holds the top of the paper end to end, the per-問題 ones hand over
問題1 to 問題2 to 問題4, the upload floats only where it is the only audio.
Furigana, scripts and recovered options unchanged: 255 annotations, 10 reading
questions held, "Tham khảo" gone, 32 folds and 33 word panels at 390px. Five
site pages and four papers N1-N5: no console errors, no horizontal overflow.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: The player docks at the top, and the whole-test recording is whole again
entry.content:
The player docks at the top, and the whole-test recording is whole again

Three things, and the first was my mistake twice over.

**One file really is the whole test.** Last commit I made wholeListeningAudio()
demand that every 問題 carry the file before treating it as a whole-test
recording, because only one of them does. That was evidence about the page, not
about the recording: the source embedded its player once, under 問題1, and left
the other four bare. The file is 201407N2.m4a - one .m4a, 41 minutes, the whole
sitting - so the heading it happened to be embedded under says nothing about
what is in it, and drawing it inside 問題1 hid four 問題 worth of audio behind a
heading and labelled it 問題1. Reverted.

The label went with it. "Audio for this section", beside a tag reading "whole
listening test", contradicted itself; the whole-test bar says "Full recording"
now.

**It docks at the top, not in the corner.** A player that belongs to the paper
belongs against the command bar: flush, square along the top and rounded below,
at the same width as the questions under it, so it reads as one piece of chrome
and covers the margin above the paper rather than the paper. A corner box has
to be dismissed before it stops sitting on the questions; this one never covers
anything being read, so the dock button it needed is gone.

A whole-test recording now follows you the length of the listening paper. A
per-問題 recording follows you through its own 問題 and hands over. The YouTube
upload still floats only where it is the only audio there is.

**Why the recording cannot be an <audio> element.** You asked why the player
sits there loading. The answer is not on our side, and it is worth writing
down, because the file itself looks perfectly usable:

    https://drive.usercontent.google.com/download?id=<id>&export=download
    200, content-type: audio/mp4, accept-ranges: bytes,
    access-control-allow-origin: *, 10,407,635 bytes, ftypM4A

Real audio, range requests, CORS wide open - and a browser still refuses it,
because the same response carries cross-origin-resource-policy: same-site.
CORP is checked before CORS can help: the bytes may not be embedded by another
site at all. Chrome reports MEDIA_ELEMENT_ERROR: Format error, and a fetch of
it fails outright. The note in the source said ORB; it is CORP, and it is now
recorded properly along with the probe that shows it.

So the iframe stays, playback speed and keyboard seeking stay Drive's to offer,
and a stalled player stays invisible to us - the frame is Google's and reports
nothing back. What could be done was to name the other way in: "Not playing?"
now also points at the full recording at the top of the section, on the 33
papers that have one.

Checked in Chrome at 1280 and 390. n2-2014-07: the whole-test recording docks
under the command bar at the reading measure and stays there the length of the
paper, through 問題1 to 問題5; the YouTube upload never floats. n2-2013-12,
whose own file is the one dead recording: the upload docks instead. n2-2018-12,
five recordings: 問題1 to 問題2 to 問題4 as you scroll, one at a time, the
iframe alive across every handover, and alive across the float on both widths.
Furigana, scripts and recovered options unchanged: 255 annotations, 10 reading
questions still held back, "Tham khảo" still gone, 32 script folds and 33 word
panels on n2-2016-07 at 390px. Five site pages and four papers N1-N5, no
console errors, no horizontal overflow.

entry.title: The paper's own recording is the one that follows you
entry.content:
The paper's own recording is the one that follows you

You asked why the audio had gone from N2 December 2013. I had taken it.
Running build_exams.py rewrites every paper from the archived sources, and
the full-recording links are stamped in afterwards by a separate command -
so the rebuild in the last commit quietly dropped listeningFull from all 33
papers that have one, and 33 listening sections lost their player. The tool's
own docstring says "run after build_exams.py, which would otherwise write the
field away", which is exactly the kind of instruction that is one day not
followed.

Restored, and build_exams.py now calls it itself. A step that has to be
remembered is a step that will be forgotten, and this one fails silently: the
papers rebuild, the site loads, and the audio is simply not there.

**Which player floats.** The paper's own recording, always - it is the real
thing, and it is what somebody working through a 問題 is listening to. The
YouTube upload is a stand-in for the sittings whose audio was never archived,
so it goes to the corner only where it is the only audio there is; on a paper
that has its own, it stays where it is drawn, at the head of the listening
test, as one row with a Play button.

There is a player per 問題 on 47 papers, so they hand over as you scroll, and
only one is ever in the corner. Which 問題 you are on is decided at the middle
of the reading area rather than at its top edge: measured at the top, a section
counted as current until its last pixel had gone, so 問題1's recording was still
in the corner while 問題2's heading, its instruction and its own player filled
the screen - two players in view, and the floating one the wrong recording.

**One recording is not one recording for the whole test.** wholeListeningAudio()
took a single file to cover the sitting and drew it above the paper, labelled
"whole listening test". Counted across the library that is true of no paper at
all: every one of the 28 with a single file has it on exactly one of its five
or six 問題, because the source published 問題1 and stopped. So a 問題1
recording sat above 問題5 with a label that contradicted the tag beside it. It
is now drawn inside the 問題 it is a recording of, and the sections without one
say the full recording above covers them, which they already knew how to say.

**Three things that were plainly wrong to look at**, all in the same screen:

- A figure that never arrives keeps the space it was promised and lays its
  message over the hole. In an answer button there is no hole - min-height is
  0 there - so the message was being centred on a box of no height and spilled
  out of the button in both directions, over the option above and the one
  below. Four failed pictures made an unreadable pile. In flow it just makes
  the button as tall as the sentence.
- The note under a section's player was full width while the player itself was
  centred on the reading measure, so the two were on different left edges.
- The player was square along the top and rounded below, which is what a
  control docked to the underside of the command bar looks like. It does not
  dock there any more, and standing inside a 問題 that flat edge read as a box
  that had lost its lid. Also: the 60px window that crops Drive's player is cut
  for the width it has in the paper, and at the 336px it gets in the corner
  Drive draws a larger centred play button instead, so the crop took the top
  off it.

Checked in Chrome at 1280 and 390. n2-2014-07, which has its own 問題1
recording and a YouTube fallback: the Drive player floats through 問題1 and
lets go after it, the upload never floats. n2-2013-12, whose recording is the
one dead file: the upload floats, and its player is back. n2-2018-12, five
recordings: 問題1 to 問題2 to 問題4 as you scroll, never two at once, the
iframe alive across every handover. Furigana, scripts and recovered options
unchanged - 255 annotations on n2-2018-12, 10 reading questions still held,
1,407 annotations inside an opened script, 32 script folds and 33 word panels
on n2-2016-07 at 390px. Five site pages and four papers N1-N5: no console
errors, no horizontal overflow.

entry.title: Furigana on the papers, and the script under every listening question
entry.content:
Furigana on the papers, and the script under every listening question

Four things you asked for. The furigana one turned out bigger than the
report suggested.

**The whole-test recording floats.** It sits above 問題1 and used to be
gone by 2番: pausing it, or rewinding ten seconds, meant scrolling back
to the head of the section and then finding your place again. Now it
lifts out of the page once you scroll past it and parks in the corner -
bottom right on a desktop, across the foot on a phone - and drops back
into its slot when you scroll up to it. Stop dismisses it; Back to the
paper returns it.

It is the same element the whole time, only its position changes. Moving
the iframe to another parent, or drawing a second floating copy, reloads
YouTube's player and restarts a forty-minute recording from zero. A slot
holds the height it leaves so the paper does not jump underneath it. It
floats rather than pins for the reason it stopped pinning: a 16:9 frame
docked under the command bar holds the top of the screen all sitting.

**Every listening question carries its script now**, on every paper,
behind a fold that stays shut until it is asked for. It used to be drawn
only where the recording would not play, on the reasoning that a script
beside an unanswered question invites reading instead of listening -
true, and the reader's decision rather than the page's. Reading along
with a recording is how a great deal of listening is learned, and a
script that unlocks only after marking cannot be used that way at all.

It is printed as a script, too: one line per turn, the speaker held out
to the left, and without "Tham khảo:" - the source site's own Vietnamese
label - at the head of all 2,444 of them.

**The questions nobody printed.** 1,468 listening questions have four
blank options, which is not damage: 問題3 and 問題4 print nothing on the
question sheet and the choices are read out at the end of the recording.
Marked, the paper therefore said "the answer was 3" against four empty
buttons, with no way to find out what 3 had been without scrubbing back
through the audio.

They are in the transcript, because the transcript is of a recording
that reads them out. add_spoken() lifts them back - 1,368 of the 1,436
that have a transcript, with the question that was asked - and the
player shows them once the question is marked, the right one marked and
the one that was picked beside it. Before marking the buttons stay
blank, because blank is the exercise.

**Furigana.** The report was that many options have none. Measured: not
one <ruby> in 20,346 questions. Zero, on every paper, in every option,
prompt and passage - which is faithful, because the real N1, N2 and N3
papers print none either, and useless when the paper is being learned
from rather than sat. A word you cannot read is a word you cannot look
up; you do not know how it sounds.

tools/build_furigana.py reads every word of every paper with the same
tokenizer the glossary uses and stores the reading it has in that paper:
見て -> 見[み]て, 食べ物 -> 食[た]べ物[もの]. A word list rather than
marked-up text, because the words of a paper repeat - 187,683 readings,
5.6 MB, one file per paper, fetched only when somebody turns furigana
on. The base of a reading is the kanji run in front of the bracket,
which is what lets お金[かね] need no separator; all 187,683 forms
round-trip through that rule.

The ふ button in the command bar draws them, and remembers the choice.
Off by default - a paper with furigana is an easier paper, and that is
the reader's call.

Two things it will not do:

- 問題1 and 問題2 of the vocabulary booklet keep their readings back
  until the question is marked. Those ask how a word is read and how it
  is written; furigana over the stem is the answer printed above the
  question. In study mode the hold lifts on that question as it is
  answered, and goes back on if you Try again.
- A word read two ways is left bare. 人 is ひと alone and にん after a
  number; 中 is なか and ちゅう. The browser matches the list against
  the text longest word first with no tokenizer of its own, so those
  would be wrong - and wrong furigana is worse than none, because the
  reader cannot tell it is a guess and will learn it. 247 words are
  dropped for it, and a single kanji only matches standing on its own,
  so 二人 stays bare rather than becoming 二[に]人.

Measured against the tokenizer over 72,672 annotations: 82% of kanji
words get a reading, 0.34% differ from the tokenizer's, the rest are
identical. Before the two rules above it was 1.72% wrong.

Checked in Chrome. Floating player at 1280 and 390: floats, docks, the
iframe survives both, 16px clear of both edges, no console errors.
Furigana on n1-2015-07, n2-2018-12, n3-2019-12, n3-practice-4,
n4-practice-2, n5-practice-2 and n2-2016-07 - 255 to 1,636 annotations a
paper, held on the 10 reading questions of n2-2018-12 until answered,
text restored exactly on switching off, no horizontal overflow at 390.
Listening: 29 of 30 questions on n2-2018-12 carry a fold, all shut, 13
speaker turns in the one opened; "Tham khảo" gone from the page; word
meanings sit on the listening questions as well. Five site pages clean.
Question totals unchanged across the rebuild: 207 papers, 20,346
questions, no paper's count moved.

entry.title: The command bar fits on one row again
entry.content:
The command bar fits on one row again

You asked whether the bottom of each page and the wrapped Submit button
were right. Measured both.

The page bottoms are right. The gap between the end of <main> and the
footer is 40px on all thirteen page types - home, levels, library, study
hub, about, quiz, review, progress, kanji, a guide, a word list, a paper
and the 404 - with no variance at all. Nothing to do there.

The bar was not right, and the reason was almost funny. It holds one row
of controls plus the progress bar, and at 360px - a Galaxy, and most of
the Android field - English wanted 325px against 324px available. One
pixel. That pixel cost a whole row: 132px of command bar instead of 90px,
at the top of a phone screen, for every question of every paper.

It was not only English. Measured across twelve languages, seven missed
the row at 360px - Indonesian by 30px, Nepali 13, Portuguese 12, Filipino
11, Vietnamese 5, Bengali 3, English 1 - because "Submit exam" is
"Kumpulkan ujian" in one language and four characters in another. And
Indonesian missed it at 375, 390 and 414 too.

The level chip goes below 481px, the way the section label already goes
below 861px. It is 44px plus its gap, and it names the level you are
sitting - which the setup screen said, the paper's title says, and the
result says again. Nothing about answering a question depends on reading
it, which is not true of the timer or Submit beside it. Below 361px the
bar also tightens its own gaps and padding, because Indonesian wants 18px
more than the chip alone releases at 320px.

Twelve languages by five widths - 320, 360, 375, 390, 414 - all sixty on
one row. Tallest bar 97px, down from 139px.

Exam player unchanged on three papers. Passage work from the last two
commits intact: 0px overlap across 7,000px of scroll, all three touch
states still right, --psg-h still measured. Bottom gaps still 40px on all
thirteen. Lighthouse P98 A100 BP100 SEO100. CSP clean on 13.

entry.title: A finger on the passage scrolls the page again
entry.content:
A finger on the passage scrolls the page again

My own regression, from the commit before this one. I put
overscroll-behavior: contain on the passage prose to stop the page moving
while the passage was being read, and the cost was far worse than the
cure: once you had read to the bottom of the passage, a drag anywhere on
the yellow card scrolled nothing at all.

That card is half the screen on a phone, so half the screen stopped
answering a finger, with nothing to tell you to move your thumb off it.

Reproduced with a real touch gesture rather than a scroll property, at
390x844, on the passage the report came from:

    before   inner 32/32   page 1264 -> 1264   did not move
    after    inner 32/32   page 1264 -> 1585   moved 321px

Default chaining is back, and all three states behave the way a nested
scroller should on a phone:

    read to the end        page takes over, moves 321px
    unread                 the drag reads the passage, page holds still
    short enough to fit    no scroller, page moves 310px

The fixes from the previous commit are intact: whole-line cuts at 9, 6, 4
and 7 lines across four screen sizes; nothing painting over the passage
across 7,000px of scroll; --psg-h still measured at 394px and questions
still landing clear of it. Exam player unchanged on three papers.

entry.title: The passage stays under its own lid
entry.content:
The passage stays under its own lid

Three faults in one card, all of them visible in a reading block on a
phone, all measured on N3 Practice Test 27.

The question was painted over the passage. .q-passage is sticky and had
no z-index, so it was painted in document order and the question block
below it - later in the DOM - was drawn on top of the thing that was
supposed to be staying in view. The question head began 82px above the
bottom of the passage and covered it: passage text appeared to run on to
the question's grey background, and the flag ended up sitting in the
middle of a sentence. Scanning 7,000px of a reading section, the worst
overlap was 82px; it is 0 now.

Every passage was sliced through the middle of a line. The cap was 42vh,
which is a number with no relationship to the text: it left a 312px text
area against a 32px line-height - 9.75 lines - so the tenth row of
characters was always cut in half horizontally. It reads as a broken
page, not as "there is more below". The cap is counted in lines now, and
lands on a whole one at every size tested: 9 lines on an upright phone,
6 in a 600px window, 4 on a phone held sideways, and on a desktop the
passage simply fits.

The label and the Word meanings button scrolled away with the text. They
were deliberately put at the top so a sticky box could not strand them
out of reach, and then the box's own inner scroll stranded them anyway,
halfway up a paragraph. The prose scrolls now and the box does not, so
they stay where they were put.

A fade marks the cut while there is more under it, and clears the moment
there is not - a fade that stayed after you reached the end would be
telling you something untrue. Jumping to a question now clears the
pinned passage too: its height is measured into --psg-h as each block is
built, rather than guessed, because the cap changes with the screen.

Exam player unchanged on three papers against the previous commit. The
section switcher added in the last commit still behaves. Lighthouse P98
A100 BP100 SEO100. CSP clean on 13.

entry.title: A way out of a section, where the section ends
entry.content:
A way out of a section, where the section ends

You were right, and it is worse than it looked. Measured on N3 Practice
Test 4 with all four sections chosen: the section switcher is drawn once,
230px down a page that is 20,234px long, and it is static. Work through
Language Knowledge, reach the end, and the only control that moves you to
Reading is 18,586px behind you. What meets you at the bottom is "Mark
this section" and "Submit exam".

And once a section was marked it was a dead end: that branch drew "End of
paper" and a review hint and nothing else - under a comment in this file
promising "nothing to submit here, just the way on to the next one". The
promise was written; the control never was.

The switcher is drawn again at the foot now, under a rule and a line
reading "Go to another section", so the two answers are separated: the
buttons above finish this section, the row below leaves it. The section
you are on is disabled rather than hidden, so the row keeps its shape and
you can see where you have been. It appears in all three end states -
still working, section marked, whole sitting reviewed - and not at all on
a single-section sitting, where there is nowhere else to go.

Not pinned to the screen, which is what you suggested. Pinning would
spend 44px of every phone screen across all 20,000px of scrolling to
serve a need that arises once, at the end - which is exactly where this
is instead. The copy at the foot is a plain group of buttons rather than
a second tablist: two tablists driving the same content is a confusing
thing to hand a screen reader. Both copies refresh together, so the
per-section counts cannot drift apart.

Verified on N3 Practice Test 4, four sections: at the bottom the row is
on screen with Language Knowledge disabled and Reading and Listening
live; pressing Reading switches section and lands at the top; marking a
section leaves the row in place instead of a dead end; top and foot
counts read identically. A one-section sitting has no row and still ends
in "Submit exam". Japanese reads ほかの科目へ.

Twelve languages, 442 keys each. Exam player unchanged on three papers
against the previous commit. Lighthouse P98 A100 BP100 SEO100. CSP clean
on 13.

entry.title: Build a row's mark buttons when the row arrives
entry.content:
Build a row's mark buttons when the row arrives

A word list is up to 3,760 rows and each was given a checkmark-and-cross
pair at load - three elements a row, 11,250 of them, for a control most
readers touch on a couple of dozen words. On n1-words that was 30,090 DOM
nodes against 18,807 elements of shipped HTML: a third of the page
existed to offer a button nobody had asked for yet.

They are built when the row comes near the viewport now, which is the
deferral the rows already get for layout - the stylesheet hands
off-screen rows to content-visibility, and this hands them their buttons
on the same terms, a screenful ahead of the scroll. Focus and click fill
a row too, so a row reached by keyboard or by a screen reader is never a
row you cannot mark. Without IntersectionObserver every row is built as
before. Only word lists have marks; kanji and grammar rows never called
markButtons and are untouched.

What it did NOT do is move the Lighthouse score. n1-words is P86 before
and P86 after, LCP 3.8s both, measured against the previous commit on a
second server. That number is set by downloading and parsing 727 KB of
HTML, which happens before any of this runs, so it was never going to
move - my reasoning about which nodes were costing the score was wrong.

What it did do, averaged over three runs at 4x CPU throttling:

    DOM nodes           30,092 -> 18,842    -37%
    layout            1,193ms -> 861ms      -332ms
    style recalc        269ms -> 229ms       -40ms
    a keystroke in the search box
                         47ms -> 34ms        -28%

So it is a third off the work of scrolling and filtering a long list on a
mid-range phone, and nothing off the first paint.

Pagination was the alternative and it is the wrong trade: rel=next/prev
has been unsupported since 2019, so eight pages of 470 words would
compete with each other instead of ranking as one list, and the page's
own search, its four filters and find-in-page all work across the whole
set today. P86 is what a crawlable 3,760-word list costs, and it is worth
paying.

Verified on n1-words: marking a word saves to storage and restyles the
row; the Known and Still-learning filters each show their one word with
its control; unmarking from inside a filter works; returning to All
rebuilds 3,759 rows with 9 controls and the first row markable; a search
narrowing to 22 rows leaves them markable. No page errors. CSP clean on
13.
